issue_context.title: Window function panicked when partition by NULL
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

1. What did you do?
If possible, provide a recipe for reproducing the error.

```
CREATE TABLE t1 (a int, b float);

INSERT INTO t1 VALUES
   (4,12),(5,2),(9,14),(12,10),(6,8),(5,7),(2,15),(2,15),(15,11),(14,5),(14,240),
   (1,10),(14,5),(5,9),(1,11),(2,5),(11,9),(13,13),(6,187),(8,12),(10,12),(15,14),
   (50,4),(14,3),(166,2),(15,13),(10,12),(48,4),(13,3),(7,10);

SELECT a, b, LEAD (b, 1) OVER (ORDER BY a,b ASC) AS c FROM t1 a ORDER BY a, b, c;
SELECT a, b, LEAD (b, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY NULL ORDER BY a,b ASC) AS c FROM t1 a ORDER BY a, b, c;
```

2. What did you expect to see?

The two select return same result.

3. What did you see instead?

The second one panicked.

4. What version of TiDB are you using (`tidb-server -V` or run `select tidb_version();` on TiDB)?

 master 373317f6a55fb01f656f247e1596ef789e15ba1c

review_comments:
This test can work well without this commit.
Maybe we need to build another case?
Any specific reason why we call `buildByItemsForWindow` separately for `orderItems` and `partitionItems`?

The only reason is to get `lenPartition` since `buildByItemsForWindow` will erase some item. If we call it once for both `orderItems` and `partitionItems`. We still need to find a way to know where is the end position of `partitionItems`.
